notes.title: The Quick Play Update (v0.3.1.0)
notes.notes:
Hello, I've been figuring out a way to make playing solo with randoms better, and this update aims to move towards a solution for this problem with the new "[b]Quick Play[/b]" along with other new additions and improvements to the game.

"[b]Sessions[/b]" was an experiment that was added to be used as a tool for finding people to play with, but it seems like it didn't work at all and mostly ended up being accidentally created when trying to host a lobby. With that being said, I'm not removing the "Sessions" yet, though it's now been renamed to "Events" and the Create Event button was moved under the "Host" button to avoid confusion.

This update introduces "[b]Quick Play[/b]", which can be entered from the Main Menu. The previous "Play" button is now renamed to "Custom Game" and is placed under the new "Quick Play" button. The "Custom Game" menu works the same way it did before.

I wanted to give players more reason to play solo and make it much easier to get into a game with this new mode. Entering "Quick Play" puts you in your own Prison, a place where your progress is saved and combined from the games you play in "Quick Play". Starting the game here puts you in a match-making queue, which will automatically join an active game or create a new one. Another big difference is that the game won't end for everyone if the host disconnects. Keep in mind that "Quick Play" is still early in development, so fixes and changes are to be expected. I'll be looking forward to feedback and I'm curious to see how it goes!

notes.title: The Backend Update (v0.3.0.0)
notes.notes:
Hello, hope you're doing well. First of all, I want to thank you for your continued feedback and support, it really means a lot to me and I'm very glad you're having fun with Odd Remedy! 🧡

This major update is more of a technical one as I'm changing the engine's scripting backend to Mono to make modding easier. I was making some preparations for this version since v0.2.5.2. As the previous save file format was impossible to load in Mono because of a now obsolete encoding/decoding system class that was previously used. I've now reworked the saving/loading system to use a custom binary format that works on anything. I wanted to make the transition to the new save file format as seamless as possible for everyone, so I delayed this update with the scripting backend change in hopes that most people will have opened the game once already and converted their saves. I've also added support for saving the game saves and stats to the Steam Cloud.

Starting with this v0.3 version, old save files (.ors) won't load. I've added a small guide in-game when pressing on an obsolete version to let you know how to convert the old save file if you wish to do so. You just need to opt-in to the "convert save files" in Steam's Betas tab in the game's properties window and simply run the game once (you can open the Console (press `) to confirm that the save files converted). Then just switch back to the latest version. Please let me know if you have any issues converting old save files.
